facts.summary: input:make_MultitouchItem - allocates the 0x10-byte HID item of type 1 (MultitouchItem) and returns it through *out. Only callers: the three CoreWindow pointer handlers 0x624A64/0x625084/0x625398 (6 call sites). Item layout: +0 vtable, +4 type byte = 1, +8 short x, +0xa short y, +0xc byte buttonId, +0xd byte data, +0xe byte pointerId.
facts.arm_signature: void** make_MultitouchItem(void** out /*r0*/, const int* buttonId /*r1, 32-bit load*/, const int* data /*r2, 32-bit load*/, const short* x /*r3, ldrh*/, const short* y /*[sp+0], ldrh*/, const BYTE* pointerId /*[sp+4], ldrb*/) -> r0 (== out); plain AAPCS, callee saves r4-r11; two stack arguments
facts.x86_to_arm_notes: New function for the ARM host (no x86 counterpart). Build exactly like call_game_make_mouse_event: copy the values into int/short/BYTE locals and pass their addresses; call through ARM32_THUMB_FUNCTION(image + rva). The result must be queued with the existing arm32_enqueue_input (EnqueueInput 0x00587294, argument = address of the pointer slot). Validate the returned item: non-NULL, readable for 0x10 bytes, ((BYTE*)item)[4] == 1.

facts.summary: Number of touch pointer slots the game supports: Multitouch::feed accepts pointerId 0..11 (>= 12 is clamped to 11; a NEGATIVE id makes the press path fail-fast with sub_b49964 + trap at 0x5B01AE). The host must hand out ids 0..11 only.
facts.x86_to_arm_notes: Allocate the lowest free slot per active WM_POINTER contact; ignore a 13th simultaneous contact.

port_instructions: Add to win32_host.c (all under #ifdef WIN32CRAFT_ARM32): policy/option parsing in the ARM Win32CraftParseHostOptions (--input, --touch-api, --osk, --input-log + env WIN32CRAFT_INPUT/WIN32CRAFT_TOUCH_API/WIN32CRAFT_OSK/WIN32CRAFT_INPUT_LOG), queue_touch_event after the ARM queue_mouse_event, the touch core block before window_proc, the OSK block after the fake InputPane, wiring in Win32Bootstrap/arm32_boot_run_loop/game_requests_relative_mouse as listed in touch_host.md section 4.

queue_touch_event(slot, buttonId, data, client_x, client_y): arm32_input_target(&handler); arm32_scale_pointer_to_buffer(&x,&y); clamp 0..32767; int b=buttonId,d=data; short sx,sy; BYTE pid=slot; ((void**(*)(void**,const int*,const int*,const short*,const short*,const BYTE*))ARM32_THUMB_FUNCTION(game_image + ARM_TOUCH_HOST_MAKE_MULTITOUCH_ITEM))(&event,&b,&d,&sx,&sy,&pid); require event && !IsBadReadPtr(event,0x10) && ((BYTE*)event)[4]==1; arm32_enqueue_input(handler,event).
Values: press (1,1), move (0,0), release (1,0); pointer ids are the lowest free slot 0..11 per active WM_POINTER touch contact; never pass a negative id.

window_proc: new ARM-only cases 0x0245/0x0246/0x0247/0x024C -> arm32_touch_pointer_message (return 0 if consumed else DefWindowProcW); 0x0240 -> WM_TOUCH fallback; 0x001F WM_CANCELMODE releases touches. For WM_POINTERCAPTURECHANGED lParam is an HWND, not a position. Positions come from (short)LOWORD/HIWORD(lParam) of DOWN/UPDATE/UP (screen pixels) -> ScreenToClient -> clamp -> arm32_scale_pointer_to_buffer. Only PT_TOUCH (GetPointerType == 2) is consumed; mouse/pen/touchpad pointers go to DefWindowProcW so the legacy mouse path is unchanged.

game_requests_relative_mouse (ARM): return host_relative_requested && !arm32_input_touch_active(); this single gate keeps update_mouse_capture from capturing/clipping/hiding the cursor and keeps HIDController+0xa0 at 0 while the last input was touch.
Never call EnableMouseInPointer. Disable touch feedback with SetWindowFeedbackSetting (types 1,7,8,9,10,11) and the MicrosoftTabletPenServiceProperty window property; log failures only.

OSK: split arm32_input_pane_try into try_show/try_hide; show = launch TabTip.exe (SHGetFolderPathW CSIDL_PROGRAM_FILES_COMMON 0x2B + \microsoft shared\ink\TabTip.exe) or ITipInvocation::Toggle when the IPTip_Main_Window window is hidden; hide = PostMessageW(IPTip_Main_Window, WM_SYSCOMMAND, SC_CLOSE, 0); eligibility by --osk; OccludedRect from GetWindowRect of that window converted to buffer pixels.

install_arm32_input_hooks: add the MultitouchItem factory to its game_functions[] sanity table. Copy this file into place, run gen_constants.py (emits ARM_TOUCH_HOST_*) and verify_constants.py; package last. Add start_touch.bat / start_mouse.bat to tools/make_arm32_device_package.py and the option rows to ARM32.md.
open_questions: What sets ScreenController+0x24c (input mode) to 2 and which events/state make the game choose the touch HUD? Not traced here; if queued type-1 items do not switch the HUD on device, the missing trigger is game-side (possibly also a dependency on HIDController+0xa0/0x25 or on the Multitouch state arrays at 0x019159BC).

In the stock pressed handler the mouse branch under HIDController+0xa0 != 0 also emits a (1,1) MultitouchItem (0x624CEC); the host's mouse path never did. Is that relevant for mouse gameplay or only for touch-emulated UI interaction?
Producer of the UI variables $touch_supported / $keyboard_and_mouse_supported (struct bytes at +0x50 / +0x4c read in sub_287fbc) - decides which control hints/settings pages are shown.
